docs/architecture/security-invariants.md invariant 1: every tenant-owned row is protected by application authorization AND effective PostgreSQL RLS

gozleme_app has DML on the tables through the foundation default privileges (data-model.md header)

docs/specs/002-organizations/progress.yaml decision 'GOZ-0002-IF-01 row-level security exception' (maintainer, 2026-11-15): accepted with conditions; deploy/helm/gozleme/README.md Organizations bullet: do not cut a release before GOZ-0003
findings.recommendation: Maintainer explicitly acknowledges the interim invariant-1 exception at GOZ-0002 PR review, and confirms that GOZ-0003 runs before any other spec that adds tenant-owned data and that no release or tag is cut while the exception is open. GOZ-0003 enables RLS on all three tables and adds them to its catalog test. GOZ-0039's release gate verifies effective RLS on every tenant-owned table. No spec may claim RLS protection before GOZ-0003 merges.
findings.disposition: human-decided 2026-11-15: accepted with conditions. (1) GOZ-0003 is the next spec that adds or touches organization-scoped data; GOZ-0040, which adds only global tables, may precede it. (2) No release or tag until GOZ-0003 lands. (3) The GOZ-0039 release gate verifies RLS on every organization table. The conditions are stated in spec-0003.md, spec-0039.md and spec-0040.md.

findings.title: The implementation depends on access paths that cross tenants before any tenant is known; a naive per-tenant RLS policy would break them or tempt trust in caller-set settings
evidence: src/Gozleme.Api/Organizations/OrganizationEndpoints.cs:51-70 ListAsync reads every memberships row of the account and joins organizations
src/Gozleme.Api/Organizations/OrganizationAccess.cs:17-25 FindMembershipAsync is the check that establishes the tenant; it reads memberships by (organization_id, user_id)
OrganizationEndpoints.cs:296 redemption finds invitations by code_hash FOR UPDATE before the organization is known, then inserts a membership (:312-320)
OrganizationEndpoints.cs:72-92 creation inserts the organization and its first membership in one SaveChanges
OrganizationEndpoints.cs:173 removal locks the organizations row FOR UPDATE
OrganizationEndpoints.cs:151-155 the member list joins the global users table for emails
src/Gozleme.Api/Identity/OperatorCommands.cs:122-150 seed resets the Seeded Demo Org as gozleme_app with no HTTP request (R3-19 operator/tenant separation)
findings.recommendation: GOZ-0003 designs RLS that keeps these paths working: an account-scoped visibility rule on memberships as well as the tenant rule; a redemption path where possession of the 160-bit code is the proof; creation inserting a new tenant; and a defined operator context for seed. The account identity used by RLS comes from the authenticated principal, set by the application in the same transaction. Tests prove that a forged or stale setting cannot read another account's memberships or invitations.

findings.recommendation: GOZ-0004 keeps the membership check first, so non-members still get identical 404s. It adds the permission check after it, which may answer 403 forbidden to members. The rule that gives existing members their initial roles is chosen with the maintainer during GOZ-0004 clarification, never inferred.

findings.title: Removing a member does not revoke the open invitations that member created, so a removed account can rejoin with a code it minted earlier
evidence: OrganizationEndpoints.cs:158-210 RemoveMemberAsync deletes only the memberships row and does not touch invitations
OrganizationEndpoints.cs:296-320 redemption accepts any open code for a non-member, including the account that created it
spec.md FR-017 requires removal to take effect on the next request, which it does; US3-5 allows rejoining with a new valid invitation; no requirement covers the removed member's own outstanding codes
Mitigation today: any remaining member sees open invitations with their creator (FR-012) and can revoke them manually
No test covers this case (MembershipTests.cs, InvitationTests.cs)

Corrected at cc1e518: OrganizationEndpoints.cs:196-215 revokes the departing account's open invitations FOR UPDATE inside the removal transaction under the organization row lock (revoked_by = acting member) and writes audit 1104 for each after commit; spec.md FR-015 updated; MembershipTests.Removing_or_leaving_revokes_the_departing_accounts_open_invitations covers removal, leaving, an untouched other member's code and the audit record
findings.recommendation: Preferred: a bounded GOZ-0002 correction. Remove and leave revoke, in the same transaction, the open invitations created by the departing account. Set revoked_by to the actor and emit audit 1104 for each one. Add an integration test showing a removed member cannot rejoin with its own earlier code. Alternative: accept this as an interim residual that GOZ-0004 must close; the GOZ-0004 prompt already carries the obligation either way.
findings.disposition: human-decided 2026-11-15: fix in GOZ-0002; corrected at cc1e518 (FR-015, T048, test). The GOZ-0004 prompt now builds on this behaviour. The correction introduced a lock-order issue, tracked as GOZ-0002-IF-20.

evidence: OrganizationAccess.cs:17-25 reads membership from the database on every request; MembershipTests.Removal_takes_effect_on_the_next_request_without_signing_the_member_out

findings.recommendation: GOZ-0023 makes any cached permit, receipt or decision that depends on membership or roles invalidate on removal, leaving, joining and role change, and tests that a removed member's earlier permit cannot authorize. GOZ-0028 lockfile revalidation inherits this through its GOZ-0023 prerequisite.

findings.title: The IF-04 correction adds an organization-then-invitation lock order in removal that can deadlock with redemption, and redemption's broad DbUpdateException catch then reports a false 'alreadyMember: true'
evidence: OrganizationEndpoints.cs:173 removal locks the organizations row FOR UPDATE, then :200 locks the departing account's open invitations FOR UPDATE (new at cc1e518)

OrganizationEndpoints.cs:313 redemption locks the invitation row FOR UPDATE first. Its SaveChanges (:340) inserts a memberships row, whose foreign key check takes FOR KEY SHARE on the same organizations row; PostgreSQL makes FOR KEY SHARE conflict with FOR UPDATE. The two paths take the locks in opposite orders.

Interleaving: redemption locks invitation X (created by the departing member), removal locks the organization, redemption's insert waits on the organization lock, removal waits on X. PostgreSQL aborts one transaction with 40P01. Before cc1e518 removal never locked invitations, so this cycle could not occur.

If removal is the victim: DatabaseUnavailable.cs:44-49 maps only connection failures and 57P* to 503, so the 40P01 PostgresException is unhandled. The API returns 500, the web helper shows 503 and the member stays.

If redemption is the victim: OrganizationEndpoints.cs:342-347 catches every DbUpdateException as 'a concurrent redemption made this account a member' and returns 200 {alreadyMember: true, organizationId} although nothing was committed. The same misreport applies to any other DbUpdateException, not only the unique-key race it was written for.

Both outcomes fail closed: no membership is created, and the invitation is revoked or stays open. The cost is a misleading response or a 500, not a breach. No test covers concurrent removal and redemption of the departing member's code (MembershipTests.cs, InvitationTests.cs).
findings.recommendation:
Bounded GOZ-0002 correction:
(1) Narrow the redemption catch to a unique violation on the memberships primary key (PostgresException SqlState 23505). Let anything else propagate.
(2) Give redemption the same lock order as removal. Read the invitation's organization_id by code_hash without a lock. Lock that organization row (for example FOR KEY SHARE or FOR SHARE, which waits for an in-flight removal), then SELECT … FOR UPDATE the invitation and re-check that it is open. Alternatively, removal could take the invitations with SKIP LOCKED, but that leaves the residual of an aborted redemption keeping the code open, so it is not preferred.
(3) Add a concurrency integration test: remove a member while its code is being redeemed. Assert that no 500 is returned, no false alreadyMember is reported, and the end state is either joined-then-removed-with-code-revoked or revoked-and-refused.
Then re-run the demo and re-analyse. GOZ-0003's prompt now records the single lock order for its RLS design.
findings.disposition: code-fix-needed: GOZ-0002 bounded correction (redemption lock order, narrowed catch, concurrency test); GOZ-0003 prompt note applied
